articles.title: GPT-6 Astra
articles.content:
GPT

Astra

Update on September 29, 2026:Learn about OpenAI's latest model:GPT‑6 .1 Sol⁠.

Update on September 22, 2026:We are expanding our GPT‑6 family with GPT‑6 Sol and GPT‑6 Luna.Learn more.

We’re introducing GPT‑6 Astra, the world’s most intelligent and aligned model.

GPT‑6 Astra brings together years of research and big bets across pre-training, reinforcement learning, and alignment. Astra is state-of-the-art on computer use, browsing, software engineering, cybersecurity, science, and professional work. Astra saturates FrontierMath Tier 4 with a 98% score, having already helpedsolve long-standing open problems⁠in mathematics. Astra also saturates ARC-AGI-3 with a 99.9% score and ExploitBench with a 100% score. It also sets a new frontier on computer and browser use, handling the most demanding professional work with unmatched speed, accuracy, and judgment.

GPT‑6 Astra is rolling out today to a limited set of organizations and over the coming days will become available to all ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users, as well as through the OpenAI API, Microsoft Azure, and AWS Bedrock.

Astra is our most aligned model, with substantial improvements in understanding user intent and model behavior—you can delegate tasks with greater confidence in Astra’s judgment. As one way that we test  this, we built a new evaluation informed by the Hugging Face incident that evaluates whether a model facing a difficult or impossible task will go beyond its intended scope. Compared to GPT‑5.6 Sol, which without production safeguards went beyond the authorized target 48% of the time, GPT‑6 Astra did this in 0% of cases.

GPT‑6 Astra marks a new frontier in the speed, accuracy, and safety of computer use. It can take care of tedious tasks like filling out online forms, updating customer records in a CRM, and organizing your calendar. It can conduct online research and draft summaries in your email or in your document editor. It can analyze scientific data, generate plots, create a website, and run frontend QA checks to make sure all the features on that site work. It can help you autonomously install and test software, and troubleshoot problems you see on screen. These improvements are also reflected in our state-of-the-art evaluation results.

These improvements also result in significant efficiency gains in real knowledge-work tasks. In latency simulations on OSWorld 2.0, Astra achieves higher computer-use performance in about 47% less time per task than GPT‑5.6 Sol, scoring 72.6% at roughly 40 minutes per task, compared with 65.7% at roughly 75 minutes.3

GPT‑6 Astra’s computer-use capabilities can be seen in outputs across domains, including game development, electrical engineering, and everyday knowledge work:

Alongside Astra, we are also updating the Codex harness to significantly improve the speed of computer use. Combined with Astra’s efficiency, this translates to a 1.9x faster task completion compared to the current GPT‑5.6 Sol experience, on the Mind2Web benchmark. The model’s improvements on speed mean it can take on many time-consuming life tasks for you, faster than you can.4

GPT‑6 Astra pairs advances in computer use with targeted training for professional environments, to help tackle complex work tasks. It combines the intelligence required for complex problems with the ability to carry out multistep workflows and produce polished documents, spreadsheets, and presentations.

GPT‑6 Astra is our best model for adhering to existing templates and producing slides that are well laid out and succinctly convey key points with a structured narrative. It creates clear, well-structured documents, presentations, spreadsheets, and analyses that follow your templates and match your writing and visual style. Astra is also trained to specifically pull only the context that matters into outputs, instead of repeating information unnecessary for the work at hand. All this means it can output more immediately usable artifacts that match your business context and standards.

GPT‑6Astra also brings stronger visual judgment to the websites, games, applications, and renderings it builds. WithSites⁠(opens in a new window)in ChatGPT, Astra can create, host, and share websites, web apps, and games directly from a prompt.

When instructions leave room for interpretation, GPT‑6 Astra is better than previous models at making the right call. It uses context to fill in routine gaps and asks focused questions when the answer could change the outcome. In Codex, it can ask asynchronously while continuing work that doesn’t depend on your reply. If you don’t respond, it proceeds with sensible assumptions where appropriate, but waits for your input on consequential decisions.

The examples below show how Astra collaborates on everyday tasks where missing information can materially change the answer.

Astra is also better at staying oriented as a task evolves. Earlier models sometimes treated steering messages as a new goal, losing track of the original request or earlier constraints. Astra incorporates new requirements, changes course when asked, and answers side questions without dropping the broader task.

GPT‑6Astra is the best model for software engineering to date.

With Astra, we’re introducing a new way for Codex to preserve and retrieve context when the context window fills. Historically, models have used compaction to summarize work during long sessions, such as when debugging complex issues or tackling large refactors. Each compaction can leave out details about why a fix failed or how a component behaves. In Codex, Astra can keep notes across context windows, preserving accumulated details without repeatedly compressing them into a single summary. Earlier context windows remain searchable, so Astra can find requirements or test results from previous messages and tool outputs—even if that information wasn’t captured in its notes. You can enable this experimental feature in yourCodex config.toml,⁠(opens in a new window)and it will become the default for Astra in the coming weeks.

GPT‑6 Astra is a major advance for scientific discovery, mathematics, and health. Today, we’re sharing two further results on the gaps between prime numbers.9,10

Astra also sets new records across a suite of math and scienceevaluations.

Astra can help with the practical work behind scientific discovery. By combining scientific reasoning with computer use, it can work directly in specialized software to inspect data and explore results, helping researchers assess the evidence and decide what to investigate next.

As we discussed in oursafety update⁠, Astra is a significant jump in cyber capabilities and meets theCritical thresholdin cybersecurity under ourPreparedness Framework. Its ability to identify and develop zero-day exploits can help defenders find and patch weaknesses, but it also creates a need for stronger safeguards. To understand how far these capabilities extend, we ran Astra on internal and third-party expert evaluations.

We first tested the model without production safeguards on ExploitBench and ExploitGym, which evaluate whether models can turn known software vulnerabilities into working exploits. On ExploitBench, Astra achieved a perfect score of 100%, compared with 78.5% for GPT‑5.6 Sol, our previous frontier cyber-capable model. On ExploitGym, Astra reached a 42.4% success rate, compared with 30.3% for GPT‑5.6 Sol, while using substantially fewer output tokens.13

Given concerns that exposure to historical software vulnerabilities may have affected benchmark results, we also evaluated Astra on two novel benchmarks. For one, we built an internal “ExploitBench (June–August 2026)” evaluation to test exploit development using vulnerabilities from the previous three months.14Astra achieved substantially higher arbitrary code-execution rates than GPT‑5.6 Sol on this dataset while using far fewer output tokens. During the evaluation, Astra even discovered and used two previously unknown zero-day vulnerabilities. We are disclosing both vulnerabilities to their maintainers.

We also tested Astra on SRE-Bench15, a benchmark that measures whether models can reverse engineer software binaries to understand its core logic without access to raw source code. Astra solved 88.0% of tasks in a single attempt and 99.2% within four attempts, compared with 55.9% and 68.7% for GPT‑5.6 Sol, respectively.

Beyond benchmarks, expert-led assessments found that Astra, when run without production safeguards, could use previously unknown vulnerabilities to achieve arbitrary code execution in hardened browsers and create privilege-escalation exploits for hardened operating-systems.

As we discussed inThe Defender’s Window, frontier cyber capabilities can help defenders find weaknesses faster, but they also make those weaknesses easier to exploit, raising the urgency for defenders to adapt. With the version of Astra launching today, defenders can use it to complete tasks such as secure code review and patching.

However, Astra will refuse to comply with more advanced cybersecurity tasks such as creating proof-of-concept exploits for vulnerabilities. ThroughOpenAI Daybreak⁠, we plan to expand access and roll out less restrictive safeguards in the coming weeks. This will enable more defensive workflows, including vulnerability and proof-of-concept validation, malware analysis, and detection engineering.

We have also strengthened our protections against potential cyber misuse, building upon our safeguards stack for GPT‑5.6 Sol. These include stronger model robustness to better withstand potential jailbreaks and more context for our monitoring systems. We have continued rigorous internal and external testing, including automated evaluations with ourinternal red-teaming attackers. More details about our cyber safeguards and testingare available in the Astrasafety overview⁠andsystem card⁠(opens in a new window)..

articles.summary: OpenAI는 사전학습·강화학습·정렬 연구를 결합한 GPT-6 Astra를 소개하며 컴퓨터 사용, 소프트웨어 개발, 과학 및 전문 업무 성능을 강조했다. 회사 발표 기준 FrontierMath Tier 4에서 98%, ARC-AGI-3에서 99.9%, ExploitBench에서 100%를 기록했으며, 특정 권한 범위 이탈 평가에서는 이탈 사례가 없었다고 밝혔다. ChatGPT 유료 이용자와 API, Azure, AWS Bedrock으로의 제공 계획은 업무 자동화와 기업 시스템 통합 측면에서 중요하다. 다만 수치는 제공사의 평가이며, 자료에 9월 후속 모델 안내가 함께 있어 Astra를 현재 최신 모델로 단정할 수는 없다.

articles.title: DeepSeek Just Released V4.1-Flash-1017, Scores 77.0 on DeepSWE, Opens Search API
articles.content: DeepSeek has just released DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017, a new checkpoint of its V4.1-Flash model. It is live on the DeepSeek website, app and API. DeepSeek claims stronger scores, faster task completion and shorter outputs than the September V4.1-Flash release. The company calls it a Pareto improvement in performance and cost. Alongside it, DeepSeek opened its Search and Fetch APIs to every developer. For agent builders, that means a cheaper coding model plus a first-party web layer behind one API key. TL;aDR Size: 552B backbone parameters plus 196B Engram parameters. It activates 8B parameters per token in prefill and 16B in decode. Context is 1M tokens, with up to 384K output tokens. Runs on: DeepSeek API as deepseek-flash. September V4.1-Flash weights (763B parameters, FP8) are MIT-licensed on Hugging Face. Hardware requirements and 1017 weights: Not disclosed. Performance: Beats the previous V4.1-Flash on all 11 benchmarks DeepSeek reported, by 2.0 to 11.1 points. Best: 77.0 on DeepSWE v1.1, above Claude Opus 5 (74.0) in DeepSeek’s table. Worst: 42.6 on HLE without tools, versus 56.3 for Claude Opus 5. What is DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017? DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 is an updated post-training checkpoint of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, served through the deepseek-flash model name. The architecture details below come from the V4.1-Flash technical report. DeepSeek team states that DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 uses reinforcement learning with self-feedback for end-to-end project work. Its examples run from game creation to 3D modeling. It is tuned for DeepSeek Harness, Tencent CodeBuddy and WorkBuddy. DeepSeek recommends DeepSeek Harness v0.2.1-rc.1 or later. How does the V4.1-Flash architecture work? V4.1-Flash is a multimodal Mixture-of-Experts model with 40 Transformer layers. They split into a 20-layer causal encoder and a 20-layer decoder. Causal Encoder-Decoder (CED): Decoder global KV is projected from the final encoder hidden states. This nearly halves prefill compute. Compressed Sparse Attention 2 (CSA2): Layers run in Full, Reindex or Reuse mode. They share main KV and indexer keys across layers. FP4 main KV cache: Global KV drops to 890 bytes per token, about 1/4 of V4-Flash. SWA Bounded Replay: Persistent KV cache shrinks to roughly 1/8 of V4-Flash. Reasoning effort: A 1 to 100 scalar. The API tiers low, high and max map to 50, 75 and 100. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 benchmarks All scores below are DeepSeek’s own figures. DeepSeek ran Terminal-Bench 4.0 in Claude Code and DeepSWE in Mini-SWE-V2. ZeroBench-main uses Pass@5. articles.title: StepFun Releases Step 5 Preview Open Weights: 600B MoE, 27B Active, 1M Context
articles.content: StepFun has released Step 5 Preview as open weights. FP8 and BF16 checkpoints are live on Hugging Face and ModelScope. Step 5 Preview is a sparse Mixture-of-Experts model from StepFun built for long-horizon agentic work. It has 600B total parameters, 27B active per token and up to 1M tokens of context. For developers, this is a new self-hostable option for coding agents, document analysis and finance workflows. TL;DR Size: 600B total, 27B active per token, up to 1M-token context. Runs on: data-center GPUs only. FP8 needs 4x B300 or 8x H200. BF16 needs 8x B300 or 16x H200. Performance: near open-weight peers GLM-5.3 and Kimi K3 on coding. Behind GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5. Best: 88.3% on AA-LCR long-context reasoning (Artificial Analysis). Worst: 33.3% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, versus 41.9% for GLM-5.3. What is Step 5 Preview? Step 5 Preview is StepFun’s flagship model for agentic work. StepFun positions it for software engineering, professional knowledge work and finance. The model navigates large codebases, coordinates multi-file changes, runs code and iterates on results. It also analyzes long documents, charts, screenshots and video to produce structured reports. The API launched September 20. Weights followed on October 14. How does the architecture work? Only 27B of the 600B parameters activate per token. StepFun’s tech team adds the internals: Depth: 92 transformer blocks in a narrow, deep design. Attention mix: gated sliding-window attention and full attention layers, interleaved 3:1. Sparse GQA: full-attention layers pick 4,096 history tokens per query, scored in blocks of 8. Speculative decoding: an MTP-3 head gives roughly 30% end-to-end speedup. Training: FP8 mixed precision, with RL on million-level verifiable agentic environments. How does Step 5 Preview perform on benchmarks? StepFun ran its own evaluations at the High reasoning setting. Rivals in its chart ran at Max effort, so the comparison is not like-for-like. Results reported on the Hugging Face card: DeepSWE v1.1: 67.7 (SWE-agent harness, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95) Terminal-Bench 4.0: 33.3 Agents’ Last Exam (ALE-CLI): 29.5 Independent numbers come from Artificial Analysis via OpenRouter. The model scores 43.7 on the Intelligence Index. It hits 88.3% on AA-LCR and 46.5% on Humanity’s Last Exam. GDPval-AA lands at 54.3%. Vals AI results show clear weak spots. SRE Bench is 0.4%. Harvey’s Legal Agent Benchmark is 9.2%. On finance, StepFun’s chart shows 66.4% on FrontierFinance. That beats GLM-5.3 and Kimi K3, but trails Claude Opus 5 at 69.7%. & How does it compare with other open-weight models? What hardware does Step 5 Preview need to run? This is a data-center model. The FP8 checkpoint alone is 650.32 GB. The full BF16 shard workflow is not yet validated end to end. vLLM and SGLang ship dedicated Docker images with OpenAI-compatible APIs. On Blackwell, expert-parallel modes use the MegaMoE backend. StepFun recommends temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95 and top_k 0. How much does the API cost? The StepFun API charges $1.00 per 1M input tokens and $2.70 per 1M output tokens. Cache hits cost $0.10 per 1M. Output pricing includes reasoning tokens. The API supports low, medium and high reasoning effort, tool calling and JSON Schema output. Key Takeaways 600B MoE, 27B active, 1M context, now open weights in FP8 and BF16. Smallest listed self-host setup: 4x B300 GPUs with FP8. Best independent score: 88.3% on AA-LCR long-context reasoning. Weakest spot: 33.3% on Terminal-Bench 4.0. API costs $1.00 in and $2.70 out per 1M tokens. articles.title: Meet Kyutai REKI: The 2.4B VLA Model Bringing Efficient Memory to Robot Manipulation
articles.content: Kyutai, with Inria and École des Ponts, has released REKI, a 2.4B vision-language-action model (VLA) for robot manipulation. The REKI vision-language-action model is pretrained only on public data. It also carries a cheap memory of its recent past. On three out-of-distribution benchmarks, only models about twice its size beat it. All weights are live on Hugging Face today. TL;DR Size: 2.4B parameters (2.2B Qwen3.5-2B VLM + 0.2B flow-matching action expert). Memory covers the last 3 frames, 1 s apart. Runs on: Benchmarked on 1 NVIDIA H100. 21.8 ms per action chunk, compiled, from 2 cameras at 256×256. Weights ship in BF16. No quantized variants announced. Performance: Best among VLAs pretrained on public data on LIBERO-Plus and RoboTwin Clean2Rand. Best: 90.4% on LIBERO-Plus, the top score in Kyutai’s comparison. Worst: 38.4% on RoboCasa365, well behind Xiaomi-Robotics-1 (57.4%). What is REKI? REKI is a vision-language-action model from Kyutai that maps camera views and an instruction to robot actions. It pairs a Qwen3.5-2B backbone with a 200M-parameter action expert. The expert generates action chunks by flow matching, integrated in 10 Euler steps. Robot state and flow time enter through adaptive RMSNorm. Each robot state layout gets its own small state MLP. How does REKI’s memory work? Most VLAs act on the current frame alone. Prior memory methods feed past frames to the VLM, unroll training, or add modules. Each option adds cost. REKI places memory inside the action expert instead. Before each frame’s action tokens sit 32 learned register tokens. They cross-attend the encoded prompt and views of that frame. They also self-attend the registers of earlier frames. Registers never read action tokens. So they depend only on observations, not flow time or robot state. They are computed once per frame and cached in a rolling window. The cost is small, per the project page: Reading cached registers adds 0.1 ms to a 21.8 ms chunk. The cache uses about 2 MiB of GPU memory per past frame. Training packs a 3-frame window into 1 batched pass. Memory also fixes a failure mode. Without it, arms often oscillate between 2 poses. On RoboTwin, oscillating episodes fall from 18.6% to 4.1% with memory. Kyutai attributes this to perceptual aliasing. How does REKI perform on benchmarks? REKI is pretrained once, then finetuned separately per benchmark. Scores below come from the model card and project page. LIBERO-Plus: 90.4%, ahead of Qwen-RobotManip (89.0%) and π0.5 (85.7%). RoboTwin Clean2Rand: 65.8%, behind only Qwen-RobotManip (68.5%). RoboCasa365: 38.4%, ahead of RLDX-1 (36.0%) and Qwen-RobotManip (35.9%). LIBERO (4 suites): 97.6%. RoboTwin 2.0 Easy / Hard: 85.9% / 84.6%. Pretraining helps most out of distribution. It adds 13.8 points on Clean2Rand and 30.3 under clutter. Memory adds 1.5 points on LIBERO-Plus and 5.4 on RoboCasa365. & How does REKI compare with other VLAs? The Qwen report lists π0.5 at 84.4 on LIBERO-Plus. What data was REKI trained on? The mixture holds 1.0B frames plus 12.2M vision-language samples. Real-robot teleoperation provides 639.8M frames, simulation 193.9M and egocentric human video 170.9M. Sources include DROID, BridgeData V2, AgiBot World, EgoDex and EgoVerse. Pretraining ran 200,000 steps on 32 H100 GPUs. Kyutai keeps each dataset’s native control convention rather than remapping actions. How do you deploy REKI? Six checkpoints are listed: the pretrained base plus finetunes for LIBERO, RoboTwin (2 variants), RoboCasa365 and RoboCasa-GR1. Real-robot deployment uses the LeRobot async-inference gRPC protocol. On a UR5 arm, REKI was finetuned for 3k steps (1 hour) on 50 demonstrations per task. articles.title: Evaluating Model Capabilities After Benchmark Saturation
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20667v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Rapid advances in AI capabilities are causing benchmarks to saturate. Once several models approach perfect scores, a benchmark loses its power to differentiate between them, and with it its utility for informing AI safety cases and frontier policies. Yet benchmark items produce far more information than the scores we typically extract from them: a full transcript of how each model solved the task. We investigate whether these transcripts can be used to assess model capabilities even after benchmark scores have saturated. We simulate saturation retrospectively using historical benchmark and model releases, and test whether protocols that access only correctly solved transcripts from saturated benchmarks can predict capabilities measured on held-out, unsaturated items. We evaluate representative contemporary approaches for extracting information from model transcripts: pairwise judging, single-transcript absolute scoring, and predictions from deterministic transcript features or embeddings. We find that saturated transcripts retain capability information beyond benchmark accuracy. Amongst our evaluated protocols, pairwise judging performs best, reducing prediction error by 5.3 times compared to a baseline using only saturated benchmark scores. This capability-relevant information is distributed across transcript sections, but concentrated in specific channels of information such as reasoning and tool-calls. However, the predictive power of protocols does not always generalise across distribution shifts -- for example by underestimating the capabilities of the first reasoning models introduced in early 2025. Saturated benchmarks thus retain capability-predicting signal in their task transcripts, but extending the lifetime of existing benchmarks requires methods designed to extract these signals robustly.
articles.summary: 벤치마크 점수가 포화된 뒤에도 정답에 도달한 추론 기록과 도구 호출에서 모델 능력을 구분할 수 있는지 분석한 연구다. 과거 모델·벤치마크를 이용한 실험에서 풀이 기록의 쌍대 비교는 포화된 점수만 사용하는 기준선보다 미포화 과제의 능력 예측 오차를 5.3배 줄였다. 이는 기존 벤치마크를 안전성 평가와 모델 비교에 더 오래 활용할 가능성을 보여준다. 다만 초기 추론 모델의 능력을 과소평가하는 등 분포 변화에서 예측력이 유지되지 않는 사례가 있어 견고한 검증 방법이 필요하다.

articles.title: AlphaDiana: A Measurement System for Agents in Verifiable Reasoning Tasks
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20675v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Agents pair reasoning models with harnesses that organize model calls, execute tools, load skill instructions, and retain history in memory. Understanding agent performance requires linking execution conditions to outcomes, behavior, and resource use. We introduce AlphaDiana, a measurement system with modular interfaces for datasets, agents, environments, and scorers. It preserves harness-native control loops while controlling file reuse and memory retention separately. AlphaDiana supports macro analyses of complete agents and micro interventions on agent components such as tools, skills, and memory under matched conditions. We study three open-source models and three open-source harnesses on five answer-based benchmarks, with two models also tested on two interactive benchmarks. We find that harnesses do not consistently improve the accuracy of reasoning: gains on questions unsolved by the model alone can be outweighed by losses on questions it answers correctly without tools. This inconsistency extends to component interventions: neither skill guidance nor retained history reliably improves accuracy. Behavior and output-token use must be assessed with correctness: low token entropy can accompany wrong answers, and less output per execution can mean more output tokens per correct answer when accuracy falls. AlphaDiana links answer correctness and execution status to traces and resource records for comparing agents and diagnosing failures under shared task and resource policies.
articles.summary: AlphaDiana는 모델과 실행 프레임워크, 도구, 스킬, 메모리의 영향을 동일한 조건에서 비교하는 에이전트 측정 시스템이다. 공개 모델 3종과 프레임워크 3종 등을 평가한 결과, 도구를 포함한 실행 체계가 모델 단독으로 풀지 못한 문제를 해결하더라도 원래 맞히던 문제를 틀리게 해 정확도를 일관되게 높이지는 못했다. 스킬 지침과 기록 보존 역시 안정적인 개선을 보장하지 않았으며, 실행당 출력 토큰 감소가 정답당 비용 감소로 이어지지 않을 수 있었다. 에이전트 도입 시 기능 수보다 정확도·실행 상태·자원 사용량을 함께 측정해야 한다는 실무적 근거를 제공한다.

articles.title: ARIA: Runtime Inspection and Amendment for Multi-Agent Systems
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20780v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS), a local mistake can propagate as other agents build on it, turning a correctable error into a failed task. Diagnosing completed runs or repeatedly re-executing them to search for corrections does not provide a learned policy for intervening while execution is still in progress. We present Agent Runtime Inspection and Amendment (ARIA), a framework for learning when and how to repair ongoing multi-agent executions. Our key intuition is to turn execution-verified repairs into reusable supervision, moving repair search into data construction and training so that a learned model can intervene at runtime without repeatedly testing alternatives. First, we collect over 24{,}000 successful and failed trajectories across four multi-agent frameworks, six benchmarks, and eight host models. From these trajectories, we construct the ARIA dataset, to our knowledge the first large-scale dataset pairing failed multi-agent trajectories with execution-verified repairs. It contains 3{,}953 verified repair pairs, each specifying what went wrong, where to intervene, and how execution should continue. Then, we develop the ARIA framework for MAS-agnostic runtime inspection and amendment, designed to integrate with any MAS that exposes execution trajectories and supports continuation replacement. Using verified repairs as training examples, we teach a compact model to recognize when intervention is needed and how to correct an ongoing run. The aim is to learn repair strategies that apply to related failures in new configurations, rather than merely reproduce individual corrections. Finally, the trained ARIA model demonstrates strong repair performance in both post-hoc and runtime settings, with generalization to unseen frameworks and host models. Our code is available at https://github.com/LabRAI/ARIA.
articles.summary: ARIA는 여러 에이전트가 협력하는 실행 과정에서 오류가 확산되기 전에 개입 시점과 수정 방법을 학습하는 프레임워크다. 연구진은 4개 프레임워크, 6개 벤치마크, 8개 기반 모델에서 2만4,000개 이상의 실행 궤적을 수집하고 실행으로 검증한 수정 쌍 3,953개를 구축했다. 이를 작은 모델에 학습시켜 실행 중 여러 대안을 반복 시험하지 않고도 수정을 제안하도록 했으며, 보지 못한 프레임워크와 모델에 대한 일반화도 보고했다. 코드가 공개됐고 실행 궤적 노출과 후속 실행 교체를 지원하는 시스템에 통합하도록 설계됐지만, 초록에는 구체적인 개선 수치가 없다.

articles.title: Evolving Together, Failing Apart: The Skill-Policy Co-evolution Trap in Self-Improving Agents
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20845v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Skill-policy co-evolution, in which an agent's policy model and its skill bank improve each other during training, is a promising paradigm for self-improving agents. Current evaluations score the co-evolved policy on the final bank it trained with (the delivered bank). After deployment, however, skills may be rewritten, added or removed more frequently than the policy model is retrained, leaving the policy to operate on a drifted skill bank that neither the training objective nor existing evaluation protocols address. In this paper, we first establish, through theoretical and empirical analysis, that the fragility hidden by this blind spot is not incidental. The acceptance rule these methods share (cooperative acceptance) ties a policy's competence to the bank it co-evolved with, leaving it fragile once skills drift, regardless of the implementation; empirically, sensitivity to skill drift grows as co-evolution training proceeds. We therefore introduce the CO-evolution Drift Audit (CODA), a deployment-oriented evaluation protocol that simulates skill drift and, alongside success rate under worst-case drift, introduces two new metrics: a consistency rate under meaning-preserving edits and a resistance rate to corrupted skills. Across four co-evolution methods and five benchmarks (six settings), worst-case success is 5-13 points below the peak measured for each delivered pair, erasing 52-93% of the delivered bank's gain over the no-skill baseline. CODA thus reframes the target of co-evolution, from peak performance on the co-evolved bank to the ability to harness skills however they evolve, and provides a shared standard against which future methods can be audited.
articles.summary: 정책 모델과 스킬 저장소를 함께 개선하는 에이전트가 배포 후 스킬 변경에 취약해질 수 있다는 연구다. 연구진은 의미를 유지한 편집과 손상된 스킬 등을 시험하는 CODA 평가를 제안하고, 4개 공동 진화 방법을 5개 벤치마크의 6개 설정에서 분석했다. 최악의 변경 조건에서는 성공률이 각 최종 모델·저장소 조합의 최고 성적보다 5~13%포인트 낮아져, 스킬 없는 기준선 대비 개선분의 52~93%가 사라졌다. 스킬을 모델 재학습보다 자주 갱신하는 운영 환경에서는 최종 조합의 성능뿐 아니라 변경 내성을 별도로 검증해야 함을 시사한다.

articles.title: Counterfactual Neighborhood Risk Fields: Evidence-Grounded Selective Safety for Vision-Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20679v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Representation-based safety defenses for vision-language models (VLMs) often learn to separate harmful from benign inputs, but separation alone does not establish what a risk score means or when it should be trusted. We introduce Counterfactual Neighborhood Risk Fields (CNRF), an evidence-grounded framework for selective VLM safety. CNRF constructs context-matched benign-harmful counterfactual pairs, uses their representation differences as capability-related risk directions, and estimates neighborhood support separately from risk. This separation prevents unfamiliarity from being conflated with harmfulness and enables selective intervention rather than blanket rejection. A victim-adaptive interface accommodates different safety observations across VLM architectures and routes selected requests for same-victim response review, which either releases acceptable candidates or produces constrained alternatives with reduced harmful capability. Across three VLMs and five multimodal jailbreak families, CNRF achieves 86.06-89.30% macro defense success rate while retaining substantial benign-task utility. Controlled experiments further show that query-matched references and preserved context-direction correspondence materially improve risk ranking in the low-false-positive regime. CNRF thus reframes representation-based VLM safety from learning harmfulness boundaries to constructing applicable evidence for selective risk decisions.
articles.summary: CNRF는 비전·언어 모델의 입력이 낯설다는 사실과 실제로 유해하다는 판단을 분리하는 안전성 프레임워크다. 맥락이 일치하는 무해·유해 입력 쌍의 표현 차이로 위험 방향을 구성하고, 주변 사례가 판단을 뒷받침하는 정도는 별도로 추정해 선택적으로 개입한다. VLM 3종과 멀티모달 탈옥 공격 5개 계열에서 매크로 평균 방어 성공률 86.06~89.30%를 보고하면서 정상 과제의 유용성도 상당 부분 유지했다고 밝혔다. 일괄 거부를 줄이는 접근으로 의미가 있지만, 실제 서비스에서의 효과는 공격 분포와 오탐 허용 수준에 따라 추가 확인이 필요하다.

articles.title: IneqAgent: Agentic Inequality Proving in Lean with Symbolic Computation
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20681v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Formal inequality proving requires mathematical reasoning and exact computation, often connected through intermediate lemmas and goal reformulations. We introduce IneqAgent, an agentic framework combining LLM reasoning with symbolic computation for inequality proving in Lean4. Lemma-level Monte Carlo Tree Search coordinates lemma construction, goal reformulation, and symbolic backend selection. Complementary sum-of-squares, Bernstein, and successive difference-substitution backends produce exact certificates for local Lean proof generation. The agent integrates these proofs with LLM-generated steps and uses Lean feedback to construct complete proofs checked against the original theorem statements. On four benchmarks, IneqAgent with DeepSeek-V4-Flash solves 175 of 186 problems (94.09%), achieving the highest overall success rate among the evaluated methods. Across four backbones, it achieves higher success rates at low LLM inference cost thresholds than Direct Agent using the same backbone, with lower mean inference costs over each method's successful runs. We also obtain Lean-verified strengthenings of Dittert's conjecture in dimensions four and five, and certify the Holens--Djokovic $(4,4)$ inequality, implying Merris's conjecture in dimension four.
articles.summary: IneqAgent는 LLM 추론과 기호 계산을 결합해 Lean4에서 부등식을 형식적으로 증명하는 에이전트다. 보조정리 수준의 몬테카를로 트리 탐색이 목표 재구성과 계산 백엔드 선택을 조율하고, 정확한 계산 인증서를 Lean이 검증하는 증명으로 연결한다. DeepSeek-V4-Flash를 사용한 평가에서는 4개 벤치마크의 186문제 중 175문제인 94.09%를 해결해 비교 방법 중 가장 높은 전체 성공률을 기록했다. 일부 수학적 추측의 강화된 형태도 검증했으며, 형식 검증과 전문 계산 도구의 결합이 정확도와 추론 비용을 함께 개선할 가능성을 보여준다.

articles.title: A Self-Improving Agent that Grows its Own DSL: Oracle-Free Operator Induction for Exact Question Answering
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20809v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A self-improving agent has to decide which new skills to keep, and in practice it keeps whatever earns a high reward, convinces a judge model, or compresses its library, even when the skill is wrong. That is fine until the answers have to be exactly right: over a table of transactions, a total is either right or wrong. We ask a harder question: can an agent grow what it can compute with no reward, no judge, and no answer key, and still be exactly right? A single frozen model runs two nested loops over a small, exact domain-specific language (DSL). The inner loop answers new questions only when two independently written expressions agree on every record. The outer loop discovers its own missing capability and authors an operator for it, admitted only when an independent second implementation agrees and the result obeys a conservation law, all without ground truth. The inner loop roughly triples the answerable-question set, and the outer loop self-extends on disjoint starting sets, inventing operators outside the starting closure; a no-induction control answers none of the new questions. The admission rule is empirically sound: it rejects 138 of 138 buggy operator variants under an independent reference, even one written by a different model family, where the admit-if-it-runs, self-consistency, and compression signals the field relies on admit most of them. Unmodified, the same mechanism self-extends on two further domains with unrelated schemas, business-ledger and clinical-encounter question answering, growing their answerable sets more than tenfold and nearly twentyfold. The loop transfers across model families too: run with further proposers, the gate stays sound and independent families self-extend comparably, with only the induction yield tracking each proposer's DSL fluency.
articles.summary: 보상이나 정답표 없이 고정된 모델이 도메인 특화 언어의 연산자를 확장하는 자기개선 에이전트 연구다. 질의 응답에서는 독립적으로 작성한 두 식이 모든 레코드에서 일치해야 답하고, 새 연산자는 별도 구현과의 일치 및 보존 법칙 충족을 통과해야 채택한다. 실험에서는 오류가 있는 연산자 변형 138개를 모두 거부했으며, 추가 도메인인 업무 원장과 임상 기록에서도 답할 수 있는 질문 집합이 각각 10배 이상과 약 20배로 늘었다. 정확성이 중요한 구조화 데이터 처리에 유망하지만, 제한된 DSL과 실험 도메인의 결과이지 임의의 작업에 대한 무오류 보장은 아니다.

articles.title: 20 Jev Alternatives: The Decision Models Taking On TypeSafe in 2026
articles.content: TypeSafe launched Jev on September 15, 2026. It is a decision model, not a chatbot. You define the allowed answers, and Jev returns a label, a score or a yes/no probability. In about 4 weeks, at least 20 Jev alternatives shipped. They come from Cloudflare, OpenAI, Perplexity, Liquid AI, AWS’s Strands Labs and independent developers. This guide compares each one on size, license, hardware, pricing, Jev API compatibility and published benchmarks. TL;DR Size range: 287M (GLiNER2.5-multi-Decide) to 35B-A3B (Mapika Decider). Jev’s size is not disclosed. Runs on: Encoders like Von and Laya run on CPU. 4B adapters fit a 24 GB GPU or a 32 GB Mac. Performance: Most open models trail Jev on hard reasoning. Several match or beat it on narrow classification. Best: Cloudflare Clef scores 94.20 BANKING77 F1 versus Jev’s 79.74, per Cloudflare’s own run. Worst: Von 1.2 scores 0.422 accuracy in Respan’s run, against Jev’s 0.932. What is Jev, and why look for alternatives? Jev is TypeSafe’s first ‘System One’ model. You send a state, such as a ticket or log line. You also send typed questions: Choice, Score or Noul (yes/no). Jev scores every question in one parallel pass and generates no text. TypeSafe’s docs list $0.042 per 1M input tokens, with free output. Context is 64k tokens per request. Input is text only. Weights are closed, and access runs through a waitlist. TypeSafe’s workflow evals put Jev at 67.8% agreement and 0.4 s per case. That leaves 4 gaps developers keep raising: no images, no self-hosting, no published size and no fine-tuning. The 20 models below fill some or all of them. How should you read these benchmarks? Most figures below are self-reported. The suites differ: JevBench, Decision Index, typed-decisions and Respan’s behavior benchmark. Scores across suites are not comparable. The one multi-model third-party table comes from Respan, which sells a competing model. Hosted decision APIs 1. Cloudflare Clef and Clef-flash Cloudflare announced Clef on October 1, 2026. Clef is 27B on Qwen3.8-27B with a vision encoder. Clef-flash is 9B on Qwen3.5-9B. Both are Apache-2.0 on Hugging Face and served on Workers AI. They accept text, JSON and up to 4 images per request. Workers AI pricing is $0.24 (Clef) and $0.038 (Clef-flash) per 1M input tokens. Cloudflare calls the API fully Jev-compatible. In its own run, Clef scored 94.20 BANKING77 F1 versus Jev’s 79.74. Jev still wins GPQA Diamond, 78.3 versus 48.0. 2. Liquid AI d1 Liquid AI’s d1 family has hosted d1 and d1-ultra, plus 2 open models. d1-3B (3.1B) runs on LFM2.5-VL-3B. d1-omni-600M (587M) adds audio clips up to 30 s. The open weights use the LFM Open License. Liquid’s guide calls d1 through TypeSafe’s own SDK with a different base URL. Liquid reports d1-3B at 48.57 on Decision Index 0.2.1. It also reports 8 ms latency on an RTX 4090. Hosted parameter counts and paid rates are not disclosed. 3. OpenAI Decisions API OpenAI released the Decisions API in public beta on October 6, 2026. It runs only on gpt-6-luna. It accepts text plus base64 images. Question types are predicate, choice and score. Pricing is $0.10 per 1M input tokens, with output not billed. The schema is OpenAI’s own, so it is not Jev-compatible. OpenAI claims about 10x faster responses than the Responses API. No benchmarks are published. 4. Perplexity pplx-decider Perplexity’s pplx-decider-v1-27b is a Qwen3.8-27B fine-tune under Apache-2.0. It reads text, JSON and up to 8 images per question. The API allows 128 questions and 255 options per request. The current pricing is $0.02 per 1M input tokens for v1.2 (27B). A 4B flash-v1.2 costs $0.01. On Perplexity’s 11-task panel, it scored 85.71% versus Jev’s 84.51%. Jev still won BBH, 94.27 versus 82.80. 5. meraGPT Decider 1 meraGPT announced Decider 1 on September 22, 2026. It is a hosted, closed-weight, text-only model. It allows up to 10 Choice labels and a 4,096-token context. The model page lists $0.04 per 1M input tokens. It exposes /v1/systemone and works with the TypeSafe SDK. On meraGPT’s typed-decisions run, it scored 0.768 versus Jev’s 0.727. An independent review notes its ECE of 0.180 trails Jev’s 0.144. 6. Respan Span-01 Span-01 is a behavior-scoring model, not a general decision model. It returns present, absent or not_observable probabilities. It costs $0.02 per 1M input tokens. Span-01 Lite is free. Respan claims 0.843 overall F1 on its Behavior Benchmark. Its own blog table shows a lower 0.806, with GPT-6 Sol ahead at 0.885. Size, base model and license are not disclosed. 7. Standard Thinking Standard One Standard One ships as 3B and 8B models, both open and hosted. The 8B is a LoRA on Ministral-3-8B under Apache-2.0. It reads text and images, with a 32,768-token context. It serves /v1/systemone. Hosted text pricing is $0.018 (3B) and $0.035 (8B) per 1M tokens. On JevBench public hard, the 8B scored 54.95% versus Jev’s 72.07%. It led on realistic transfer, 90.83% versus 86.67%. Both runs are publisher-measured. Open-weight Jev alternatives you can self-host 8. Together AI Tev1-4B-experimental Together trained Tev1 as a LoRA SFT of Qwen3.5-4B. It cost about $17 and 25 minutes on 37,840 examples. It picks from 2 to 24 options. The model card says the weights license is still being finalized. It answers through chat completions, not a native Jev endpoint. Respan measured 0.901 accuracy and 0.031 ECE, the best ECE in its table. Together warns its logprobs are not calibrated confidence. 9. Fastino GLiNER2.5-Decide Fastino’s GLiNER2.5-Decide is a 340M DeBERTa-v3-large encoder under Apache 2.0. It handles decisions, span extraction and relations in one pass. A 1B and a 287M multilingual variant also exist. On Fastino’s 17-domain set, the model card lists 60.2% exact match. p50 latency is 167.3 ms on a 48-vCPU Xeon. It is not Jev API-compatible. 10. Strands Labs Strands Decider 2B AWS’s Strands Labs introduced Strands Decider on October 1, 2026. It is about 1.9B: Qwen3.5-2B-Base plus a pointer head. The repo publishes 246,678 training rows and the full recipe. One RTX 3090 trains it in about 11 hours. It serves a local /v1/systemone endpoint under Apache-2.0. The v1 checkpoint scored 180 of 231 (77.9%) on JevBench public. Median latency is 115 ms on an RTX 3090. 11. Kev (Jared Palmer) Kev comes in 0.8B, 4B, 9B and 27B sizes on Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.8. Kev-4B is a LoRA plus pointer head under Apache-2.0. It supports 255 options. The TypeSafe SDK works against it unchanged. Kev-4B fits a 24 GB GPU or a 32 GB Apple Silicon Mac. Respan measured 0.833 accuracy and a 0.060 flip rate. Self-reported MMLU-Pro is 0.565 versus Jev’s 0.840. Option order can change its answers. 12. Mapika Decider family Mapika’s Decider ships 0.8B to 35B-A3B variants on Qwen3.5 and Gemma 4. A decider-2b-vision model adds images. Everything is Apache-2.0, with 32k context and /v1/systemone. On the JevBench public hard tier, decider-12b v1 tied Jev at 0.730. The 4B GGUF Q4_K_M is 2.7 GB and runs on CPU. The 4B’s ECE is 0.184 on hard items, so expect overconfidence. 13. Bespoke Labs Bespoke-Nimble-9B Bespoke-Nimble-9B is a 165 MiB LoRA on Qwen3.5-9B, Apache-2.0 on Hugging Face. The current card lists 255 choices and 8,192 tokens. It reads English text only. On Bespoke’s 324-example held-out set, Nimble scored 90.12% versus Jev’s 93.21%. Latency is about 106 ms on an H100. It trained on only 2,676 examples, and its probabilities are not calibrated. 14. Convai Innovations Laya Laya is a ModernBERT-based family with 421M English and 322M multilingual checkpoints. It is Apache-2.0 and text only. The laya-serve server exposes a Jev-shaped /v1/systemone endpoint. The typed-decisions checkpoint scored 0.766 versus Jev’s 0.727. On Banking77, it scored 0.425 versus 0.870. Respan measured 0.542 accuracy and a 0.396 injection success rate. p50 latency is 32.8 ms on a T4. 15. Von (wfzyx) Von is a 395M ModernBERT-large encoder with an option-marker head. It scores all options in one bidirectional pass. It is Apache-2.0 with an 8,192-token context. The repo reports 0.096 s p50 on 4 vCPUs and 0.023 s on an A10G. Respan measured Von 1.2 at 0.422 accuracy, the lowest in its table. Its calibration is tuned to JevBench and can mislead out of domain. 16. Open-Jev-9B (Zefan Cai) Open-Jev ships 2B, 9B and 27B adapters on Qwen3.5 bases. Open-Jev-9B adds a scalar head and fits one 16 GB GPU. It matches the /v1/systemone request shape but claims no parity. On a 231-task JevBench subset, the project reports 77.49% for 9B and 85.28% for 27B v1.1. Each candidate is capped at 4,096 tokens. Numeric and timeline tasks are weak. 17. OpenJev on DiffusionGemma (razorback16) This OpenJev reads decisions from NVIDIA’s DiffusionGemma 26B-A4B (4B active). It accepts text plus up to 8 images. It uses the same wire API, so Jev SDKs work unchanged. The project reports 87.4% on JevBench public and 30 ms p50 at 49 tokens. A free hosted endpoint gives 100M tokens per account. Self-hosting needs an NVIDIA GPU with at least 24 GB. 18. InnerJev-4B and InnerJev-27B InnerJev comes from a Fudan, Tongji and King’s College London team. It distills LLM reasoning into a single-pass decision. The paper also introduces JEVal: 11,257 instances across 36 datasets. On JEVal, InnerJev-27B scored 79.24% versus Jev’s 78.38%. Its ECE was 0.0149 against Jev’s 0.0532. InnerJev-4B scored 71.92%. Code is on GitHub; the license is not stated. 19. SemIf SemIf reads typed decisions from existing open LLMs, with Qwen3.5-4B as the default. A WebGPU demo runs quantized models in the browser. Code is MIT. On a 102-row TypeSafe subset, SemIf scored 0.845 balanced accuracy versus Jev’s published 0.883. On an RTX 3090, direct logits took 1.023 s versus 5.332 s for JSON generation. It has no Jev-compatible endpoint. 20. Rizzo Flow Riz
articles.summary: TypeSafe의 Jev 출시 이후 약 4주 동안 등장한 최소 20개 대안을 비교하며, 텍스트 생성 대신 정해진 라벨·점수·확률을 반환하는 결정 모델 시장을 조명한 기사다. Jev는 여러 형식화된 질문을 한 번의 병렬 처리로 평가하며, 대안에는 CPU에서 실행하는 인코더부터 GPU 기반 모델과 호스팅 API까지 포함된다. 티켓 분류나 로그 판단처럼 출력 형태가 제한된 작업에서는 범용 챗봇과 다른 비용·배포 선택지를 제공한다. 다만 비교 수치 대부분이 자체 보고이고 평가 체계가 달라, 특정 분류 성적을 일반적인 추론 우위로 해석해서는 안 된다.

articles.title: Value-Informed Schedule Trimming for Accelerated Sequential Monte Carlo Guidance in Discrete Diffusion
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20669v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reward-guided discrete diffusion enables test-time alignment with downstream objectives, but applying Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) guidance at every denoising step is computationally expensive. Active guidance steps require additional reward evaluations and, for gradient-based proposals, value-gradient computations. Sparse guidance reduces this cost by guiding only a subset of timesteps, but commonly used schedules are fixed heuristics whose effectiveness can vary substantially across tasks. We propose VISTA, a training-free method that automatically selects guided timesteps under a fixed budget. VISTA formulates sparse guidance as approximation of the ideal full-guidance probability path and derives an estimable upper bound on \(\ell_1\) path deviation. Using value statistics collected from a small number of full-guidance warmup generations, VISTA optimizes the resulting empirical surrogate exactly via dynamic programming. The warmup generations can be retained as model outputs, and after schedule selection VISTA has the same per-generation guidance complexity as other sparse schedules with the same budget. Across text, biological sequence, and image generation tasks, VISTA discovers task-dependent schedules and outperforms hand-designed sparse schedules in most tested settings, while approaching or exceeding full-guidance performance on several task metrics. In toxic-text generation, for example, VISTA attains a 0.99 unique-toxic ratio compared with 1.00 for full guidance while reducing post-selection per-generation latency from 204.23 s to 38.16 s, a 5.35$\times$ speedup.
articles.summary: VISTA는 보상 유도형 이산 확산 모델에서 비용이 큰 순차 몬테카를로 유도를 어느 시점에 적용할지 자동 선택하는 추가 학습 없는 방법이다. 소수의 전체 유도 예열 생성에서 얻은 가치 통계로 근사 목적함수를 만들고 동적 계획법을 통해 고정 예산 내 일정을 최적화한다. 텍스트·생물학적 서열·이미지 실험의 대부분에서 수작업 희소 일정보다 나았으며, 유해 텍스트 생성 평가에서는 일정 선택 이후 생성당 지연을 204.23초에서 38.16초로 줄이면서 목표 지표를 거의 유지했다. 추론 비용 절감 가능성을 보여주지만, 5.35배 속도 향상은 예열과 일정 선택 비용을 제외한 해당 실험 조건의 결과다.

articles.title: Confidence-Calibrated Inference Expansion for Evaluator-Guided Test-Time Reasoning
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20836v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Evaluator-guided reasoning presents a local control problem at every step: trust the current answer, return a fallback, or spend more inference. We formulate this choice as a compute-aware three-action controller, scoring terminal actions by predicted answer success and expansion by a rollout-based continuation-success surrogate, with compute cost priced explicitly. A local action-gap analysis characterizes when score errors can change a decision, while an expected regret bound accounts for errors along the realized expansion path. Guided by this analysis, we learn and calibrate action-specific confidence estimates, with local uncertainty penalties for ambiguous decisions. On held-out width expansion and revision tasks, the controller improves observed utility over calibration-selected fixed policies while reducing normalized online compute by about 30% and 16%, respectively. Across four Qwen3-8B seeds, compute is lower than fitted Q in both settings, while utility differences are small and mixed. The results frame evaluator-guided reasoning as resource allocation under uncertainty, rather than a uniformly stronger reasoner.
articles.summary: 평가기 기반 추론에서 현재 답을 채택할지, 대체 답을 반환할지, 계산을 더 수행할지를 선택하는 신뢰도 보정 제어기를 제안한 연구다. 각 행동의 예상 성공 가능성과 추가 계산 비용을 함께 평가하고, 불확실한 결정에는 국소적인 불확실성 페널티를 적용한다. 별도 평가 과제에서 보정으로 선택한 고정 정책보다 관측 효용을 높이면서 정규화된 온라인 계산량을 확장 과제에서는 약 30%, 수정 과제에서는 약 16% 줄였다. 다만 fitted Q와 비교한 효용 차이는 작고 혼재돼, 보편적인 추론 성능 향상보다는 불확실성 아래의 자원 배분 개선으로 해석하는 것이 적절하다.

articles.title: Open-world AI: a Tale of Three Requirements
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20782v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The closed world asks AI for specialized competence and lets it manufacture the iid data its theory assumes: a fixed criterion licenses collecting examples until the task is covered. The open world asks for versatility --- taking up tasks a machine was not built for, from few examples and with little prior from a human designer --- and offers data that is grouped, not shuffled. Its tasks are not known in advance, so a machine must do inference-time learning (1st requirement). Modeling tasks as sharing latent factors and decomposing the training objective, we derive two more: a *rich representation*, retaining more than iid generalization requires, and a predictive disentanglement that aligns inputs and outputs into matched low-dimensional groups. The analysis further predicts the need for a consistent inner learner, and the benefit of long contexts spanning related tasks. We test these claims on language models up to 8B, asking whether a model has a property (qualitative) rather than how much it wins (quantitative). Models that meet the requirements improve as data from related tasks accumulates; the rest degrade, and neither scale nor layer-type interleaving repairs this.
articles.summary: 새로운 과제를 적은 예시로 익혀야 하는 개방형 AI에 필요한 조건을 이론과 언어 모델 실험으로 분석한 연구다. 추론 시점 학습, 풍부한 표현, 입력과 출력을 대응하는 저차원 그룹으로 정렬하는 예측적 분해를 핵심 요건으로 제시한다. 최대 80억 매개변수 모델의 정성적 실험에서는 요건을 충족한 모델이 관련 과제 데이터의 누적에 따라 개선됐지만, 그렇지 않은 모델은 오히려 성능이 저하됐다. 긴 문맥을 제공하는 것만으로 적응이 보장되지는 않으며 표현과 내부 학습 방식이 중요하다는 시사점이 있으나, 결과를 모든 규모와 과제에 일반화할 근거는 제시되지 않았다.
